source: Def Jam, the pioneer label in hip hop, is properly at #1.
claim: Def Jam ranks first on rank-weighted chart success with 63,759 points, ahead of Young Money (52,213) and Roc-A-Fella (44,799).

source: Young Money has only been active for the past six years, and it’s at #2, exemplifying the current state of hip hop and its concentration in one place.
claim: Young Money ranks second on rank-weighted chart success with 52,213 points, and its chart entries run only from 2009-05-02 to 2015-04-18.

source: Young Money has been the top label for each of the past five years.
claim: Young Money had the highest rank-weighted chart success of any label in every year of the 2010-2015 period.

source: 10 years ago, success was spread-out among large to mid-size labels. Today, hits are concentrated among a few major labels, with the remaining distributed among smaller labels.
claim: In 2005 the five most successful labels took 33.9% of the year's rank-weighted chart success and the ten most successful took 55.8%, while in 2015 the top five took 58.5% and the top ten took 79.4%.

source: For the first time in hip hop’s history, one label has had unprecedented influence.
claim: Young Money's 27.5% of 2015's rank-weighted chart success is the largest single-year share of any label, ahead of Shady's peak of 13.0% in 2003.
Def Jam charted the most distinct tracks of any label (152), ahead of Jive (106), Roc-A-Fella (86) and Young Money (83).
Def Jam accumulated the most weeks on chart (1,925), followed by Young Money (1,322), Roc-A-Fella (1,293) and Jive (1,255).

source: Jive is crushing it with a roster that includes Boogie Down Productions, DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince, and Too $hort.
claim: In 1989, Jive had the highest rank-weighted chart success of any label (3,066 points), ahead of Capitol (2,148) and Ruthless (1,793).
